title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are seeing a mix of innovation and regulatory challenges. From military budget increases in Europe to new propulsion technologies, the landscape is as dynamic as ever.

themes.title: Military Budgets and Space Growth
themes.body: The surge in military budgets could provide a much-needed boost to Europe’s entrepreneurial space sector, but only if spending accelerates. As nations prioritize defense, the question remains whether this will translate into tangible support for emerging companies.

themes.title: Propulsion Innovations on the Rise
themes.body: Voyager's recent DARPA contract for solid rocket propellant technology underscores a renewed focus on propulsion advancements. Meanwhile, Chinese startup Mega Engine is making strides with its reusable staged-combustion rocket engine, hinting at a competitive edge.

themes.title: Regulatory Hurdles Persist
themes.body: Europe's smallsat industry continues to grapple with access to capital and regulatory challenges, stifling its growth potential. This stagnation contrasts sharply with the rapid developments seen in other regions.

themes.title: New Ventures and Investments
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C funding round highlights the growing interest in space domain awareness technologies. As the defense-tech IPO window begins to crack open, more startups may find themselves in the spotlight.
